topic: Road Map for Embedding Ethics into ChE Undergraduate Curricula
title: Road Map for Embedding Ethics into ChE Undergraduate Curricula
abstract: The author will outline a number of methodologies and a suggested subject sequencing that can be effectively used to further develop an embedded ethics curricula. This curricula will consist of definitions, examples and suggestions on where to embed ethics into any existing ABET-approved, chemical engineering undergraduate course set. The author has lectured extensively at universities on ethics and a number of ethics related subjects.

topic: Views on Ethics in Undergraduate Education
title: Views on Ethics in Undergraduate Education
abstract: Engineering programs are expected to graduate students who understand their professional ethical responsibilities. A student’s experience with ethics often begins with academic integrity. Research on student attitudes and behavior regarding academic integrity will be reviewed with suggestions to help faculty nurture a strong ethical foundation in their students.

topic: Ethical Reasoning in the Engineering Curriculum
title: Ethical Reasoning in the Engineering Curriculum
abstract: Although the provision of ethics in engineering curricula has increased in recent years, the teaching of engineering ethics remains patchy and sporadic in a number of countries. Ethics in research, on the other hand, appears to be at a more mature stage. At the same time, the number of ethical codes, codes of practice and research concordats has flourished, both nationally and internationally. The questions remain: are those codes “live”? Have those concordats resulted in an improvement of professional integrity? Is the teaching of ethics different and/or disconnected from ethics in research and in the workplace? Is ethics in chemical engineering different from ethics in other engineering disciplines? The paper analyses those questions in relation to an ever changing landscape, influenced by local and international drivers.
